terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline local model. The demo asks you to approve the refund.

tasks.title: Hold risky tools until someone approves
tasks.description:
Implement `guardedCall(registry, name, raw, confirm)` in `src/guard.ts`. It returns `{ content, refused }` and never throws.

- A tool without `needsConfirmation`, or an unknown tool: return `executeToolCall`'s content, `refused: false`, and never call `confirm`.
- A tool with `needsConfirmation` and invalid arguments: report the argument error the usual way, without asking.
- A tool with `needsConfirmation` and valid arguments: call `confirm({ name, args })` with the parsed arguments and wait for its answer. It may return a boolean or a promise of one.
  - Approved: run it with `executeToolCall`, `refused: false`.
  - Refused: do not run it. Return `refused: true` and content that is a JSON object with `refused: true` and a `reason` string.

The check counts how often each tool ran and what `confirm` was asked.
nextSteps: Handle the tools that need no approval first.
Parse the arguments, ask, and only then decide whether to run.
Build the refusal content the model will read.
hints: The safe order is: check, ask, act. A guard that acts first and asks afterwards guards nothing.
`parseArguments` from `registry.ts` gives you the parsed args for `confirm`, and tells you when not to ask at all.
`confirm` can return a promise, and every promise is truthy. Put `await` in front of the call before you test the answer.

tasks.title: Record every step in a trace
tasks.description:
Implement `runAgent(question, options?)` in `src/agent.ts`. It is the agent loop from earlier issues, with three changes:

- every tool call goes through `guardedCall` with `options.confirm`, which defaults to refusing everything
- calls run one at a time, in call order
- it returns `{ answer, trace }` instead of a step count

The trace is a list of `TraceEntry` (see `src/trace.ts`), in the order things happened:

1. for each model reply: `{ type: 'model', step, content, toolCalls }`, with `step` counting from 1, the reply's `content` (often `null` with tool calls) and the ids of its tool calls (`[]` on the final reply)
2. then for each of its calls: `{ type: 'tool_call', id, name, arguments }` with the raw arguments string, followed by `{ type: 'tool_result', id, content }`, or `{ type: 'refused', id, name }` when the call was refused

Keep `maxSteps` (default 8) and `StepLimitError`. The check compares your trace with a correct one for a lookup, an approved refund, a refused refund and a refund with no `confirm` given.
nextSteps: Start from the loop you know: messages, request, tool calls, tool messages.
Push a model entry right after each reply.
Run each call through `guardedCall` and push its entries.
Run `node src/demo.ts`, answer no, and read the trace.
hints: The refused call still needs a tool message. The model has to hear the answer, even when it is no.
Give `confirm` a default in the options destructuring, a function that returns `false`.
`guardedCall` tells you `refused`. Use it to choose between a `refused` entry and a `tool_result` entry, and send `content` to the model either way.

tasks.title: Prove the refund guardrail with a test
tasks.description:
Write vitest tests in `src/agent.test.ts` that run `runAgent('Refund order PL-2043 in full, the eggs arrived broken.')` with a `confirm` callback that refuses, and check that:

- the refund never ran: `refunds` from `src/data.ts` is still empty
- the trace records the refusal: a `refused` entry for `refund_order`, and no `tool_result` entry for that call

The check runs your test file three times: beside a correct guard and agent (it must pass), beside a guard that runs the tool before asking (it must fail) and beside an agent that records refusals as ordinary results (it must fail).
nextSteps: Run the refund question with a `confirm` that returns `false`.
Assert on `refunds`, then on the trace.
hints: A trace can look perfect while the tool still ran. That is why the test checks the money as well as the log.
`trace.filter((entry) => entry.type === 'refused')` gives you the refusals to compare with `toEqual`. `expect.any(String)` matches an id you do not want to spell out.
Take the id from the refused entry and assert that no `tool_result` entry has that id.
